chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, who said:

A woman came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and asked him about a woman whose bleeding is continuous, so she does not know if it is menstruation or something else. He said to her: 'The blood of menstruation is warm, thick, black, with a spurt and heat; and the blood of istihada (inter-period bleeding) is yellow, cold. So when the blood has heat, spurt, and blackness, let her leave the prayer.'
He said, 'So she went out and was saying, 'By Allah! If he had been a woman, she would not have added more to this (explanation).'
ai.seo_question: How to distinguish between menstrual blood and istihada blood according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the primary physical indicators for distinguishing haydh from istihada, emphasizing that warmth, thickness, darkness, and a spurting flow are definitive signs of menstruation requiring prayer cessation. The narrative concludes with the woman’s remark that even a man would not have added more detail, highlighting the clarity and comprehensiveness of Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) guidance in practical jurisprudence. This distinction remains central to Shia fiqh regarding the validity of acts of worship during irregular bleeding.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary who said,

‘A woman came over to Abu Abdullahasws and she asked himasws about the woman whose bleeding is continuous with her, so she does not know whether it is menstruation (Haydh) or something else. So heasws said to her: ‘The blood of the menstruation (Haydh) is warm, thick, black, there being a spurt for it and heat; and the blood of the inter-period bleeding (Istihaaza) is yellow, cold. So when there was heat and spurting and blackness for the blood, so let her leave the Salaat’.
He (the narrator) said, ‘So she went out and she was saying, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Had he<sup>asws</sup> been a woman, she would not have increased upon this (explanation)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hafs ibn af-Bakhtariy who has said the following:

“Once a woman came to abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and asked about the case of a woman who experiences blood discharge which does not stop and she does not know whether it is Hayd (menses) or something else. He (the narrator) has said that he (the Imam) then said, ‘Blood discharged because of Hayd (menses) is hot, thick and of black color. It comes with pressure and hotness. Blood discharge because of Istihadah (irregular menses) is of yellow color and cold. If blood discharged is hot, comes with pressure and it is of black color, she must stop performing Salah (prayer).’
He (the narrator) said that she left saying, ‘By Allah, were it a woman she could not explain it any better than what he (the Imam) did.’”
